resale_co.name: Certificate of Habitability (CH)
resale_co.issued_by: Town of Phillipsburg Office of Inspections (Inspections / Building Dept)
resale_co.lead_time: A minimum of 2 weeks is usually required
requirements: Smoke alarms: at least one working alarm on each level and within 10 feet of each sleeping area; battery alarms must be listed 10-year sealed type; wired alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms
CO alarms within 10 feet of each sleeping area (hardwired, plug-in or battery)
Fire extinguisher: 2A:10-B:C minimum, 10 pounds maximum, mounted within 10 feet of the kitchen (not near the stove), no higher than 5 feet, new or tagged
House numbers at least 4 inches, visible from all facing streets and alleys
Yard, fences, sheds, sidewalks and curbs kept free of weeds, debris and trip hazards
Exterior in good repair: no rotten wood or peeling paint, roof, siding, gutters, downspouts, chimney and foundation in good condition
Handrails on stairs with more than four risers; guardrails on porches and decks 30 inches or taller
Interior clean, walls, ceilings and floors free of breaks or flaking paint; old unused appliances, water heaters, boilers and oil tanks removed
Electrical: at least two receptacles per room, GFCI in bathrooms, kitchen counters and outside, grounded or GFCI three-prong outlets, covered boxes, no visible knob-and-tube wiring or fuse panels
Proof of professional heating system service; no plumbing leaks; approved fittings; property connected to town sewer
Other violations under the 2000 International Property Maintenance Code and town code may be cited

resale_co.how_to_apply: Email the Office of Inspections at constructionofficial@phillipsburgnj.org (buying/selling property) to request the Certificate of Habitability inspection; fees are paid before the inspection and checks are payable to the Town of Phillipsburg. Office at 120 Filmore Street, Monday to Friday 8 am to 4 pm. If violations remain at closing, the buyer can sign a notarized Affidavit of Understanding for a 180-day conditional certificate (form: https://phillipsburgnj.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Affidavit-Of-Understanding-2024.docx). No CH application form is posted.

The Office of Inspections provides this guide as a courtesy to help property owners know what is generally required to receive a Certificate of Habitability.

resale_co.notes: Phillipsburg requires a Certificate of Habitability (Code Chapter 219) for sale or transfer as well as for rentals. The fee schedule comes from Ordinance 2024-12 as posted on the town's ordinance list; the posted copy is the first-reading version (introduced June 12, 2024, final hearing set for June 26, 2024), and adoption was not confirmed from minutes, though the town's 2024 conditional-certificate affidavit uses the same $100 fee. The fee schedule for 20 or more units and commercial certificates is omitted here. The town's standard Certificate of Occupancy application (UCC F270) on the same page is for new construction, not resale. Rentals also need yearly registration and a yearly CH (rental-only). The Office of Inspections contact is a shared mailbox; no named staff contact is published. The site uses a rate limit (Wordfence), so some pages could not be re-read.

requirements: The town's Certificate of Habitability inspection checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and a fire extinguisher (see resale certificate requirements); the town's 2022 guide still lists a fire extinguisher (2A:10-B:C, max 10 pounds, within 10 feet of the kitchen, no higher than 5 feet)

authorities.how_to_apply: No smoke certificate application form or instructions are posted yet. Contact the Office of Inspections (constructionofficial@phillipsburgnj.org, 908-454-5500) to ask how to book the CSACMAPFEC inspection; it may be done together with the Certificate of Habitability inspection.

fire_cert.notes: Unsettled. The July 2026 DCA LEA Registry lists Phillipsburg (printed as 'Phillipsburg Township') as State-enforced, but DCA's state-enforced towns list (revised 7/17/2026) shows Phillipsburg WITHOUT the 'SC' (Smoke Certs) mark, so DCA does not issue smoke certificates there. On August 11, 2026 the Town Council adopted Ordinance 2026-24, which creates a Town Fire Official and sets CSACMAPFEC fees of $45 / $90 / $161. The town's Certificate of Habitability inspection also checks smoke alarms, CO alarms and an extinguisher. No town page yet explains how to book the smoke certificate or names the Fire Official; the Fire Department page lists only the volunteer Fire Chief (Rich Hay). The ordinance still says 'portable fire extinguisher' in the certificate name although P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state requirement.

other_items.label: Rental units: yearly rental registration and yearly Certificate of Habitability
other_items.detail: Rental registration ($100 per unit per the town's guide) is filed online; the CH must be renewed every year for rentals. Not needed for a sale to an owner-occupant beyond the resale CH.

other_items.label: Property must be connected to town sewer
other_items.detail: Listed in the Certificate of Habitability compliance guide.
